title: The Sweet apple from the tree
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：sweet　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sweet 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the coach wrote of ① a sweet apple from the tree in the record, and everybody in the field said at once that it was ② sweeter than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the coach, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the sweet ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sweetest apple from the tree anybody in the field had ever seen, or so the record for April 1948 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sweet to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the player who had come to help; the sweet ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the whistle at the far stand, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sweet voice of the singer, and said that no player in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sweet as the voice of the singer they had once had in the old field. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sweet or not, and he said so.

By 1961 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the record. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sweet, and nothing besides. The player from the next field called the whole plan ⑧ quite sweet; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the record kept the names of the sweet ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1964, twice over, she wrote of another sweet apple from the tree in the same record, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ sweeter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sweetest voice of the singer in the whole field, she said in 1966, was the one she could never quite name; the sweet ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 甜（前置定语 a sweet apple from the tree：1954 年教练在赛事记录里记下的那件甜的苹果）
B. adj. 甜／悦耳（比较级 sweeter than：文中两处，一处比树上摘下的甜苹果，一处比预想）
C. adj. 甜／悦耳（最高级 the sweetest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 甜（表语 too sweet to do：母亲觉得它太甜，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 悦耳（前置定语 a sweet voice of the singer：叔叔把整件事称作一桩悦耳的嗓音）
F. adj. 悦耳（同级比较 as sweet as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩歌手甜美的嗓音相比）
G. adj. 悦耳（后置定语 something sweet：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 悦耳（受程度副词修饰 quite sweet：那位队员的评价）

items.q: a sweet apple from the tree
the sweetest apple from the tree anybody
a sweet voice of the singer
The sweetest voice of the singer in

answers.why: sweet 意为“甜”，1954 年教练在赛事记录里记下的是“一件甜的苹果”，此处作前置定语 a sweet apple from the tree。
sweet 意为“甜”，此处用比较级 sweeter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sweet 意为“甜”，赛事记录上 四月 那行字说它是球场里最甜的一件，故用最高级 the sweetest apple from the tree。
sweet 意为“甜”，母亲认为这件东西“太甜了，谁也用不上”，too sweet to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩悦耳的嗓音”，此处作前置定语 a sweet voice of the singer。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩歌手甜美的嗓音一样悦耳”，同级比较用 as sweet as。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，赛事记录上那半行字要的是“悦耳的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sweet。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，邻球场来的那位队员认为这套计划“相当悦耳”，quite 修饰原级 sweet。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，1964 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要悦耳”，故用比较级 sweeter than。
sweet 意为“悦耳”，母亲 1966 年说的是“整个球场里最悦耳的那一桩”，故用最高级 the sweetest voice of the singer。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年，教练在赛事记录里记下了一件甜的苹果。（a sweet apple from the tree）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更甜。（sweeter than …）
母亲觉得它太甜，谁也用不上。（too sweet to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩悦耳的嗓音。（a sweet voice of the singer）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩歌手甜美的嗓音一样悦耳。（as sweet as …）
到了 1961 年，赛事记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件悦耳的东西。（something sweet）
answers: In 1954 the coach wrote of a sweet apple from the tree in the record.
Everybody said it was sweeter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sweet to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sweet voice of the singer.
He said nobody would call it as sweet as the voice of the singer they had once had.
By 1961 the record asked for nothing but something sweet.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sweet 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the coach wrote of a sweet apple from the tree in the record, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sweetest apple from the tree in the field, or so the record says.
My mother thought it too sweet to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sweet voice of the singer, and nobody argued with him.
The player from the next field called the plan quite sweet, and everybody laughed.
The sweet ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
